newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Poor high growns keep prices low at Colombo sale.
newsitem.headline: Poor high growns keep prices low at Colombo sale.

text.p: A decline in Sri Lanka's pricey high grown teas depressed prices at the Colombo auction on Wednesday, where 4.8 million kg were on offer, brokers said.
"Low growns were firm. The drop in prices was mainly due a decline in prices fetched by high growns," said Rohan Iddawela of brokers Forbes and Walker.
The anticipated gross auction average was down to 115 rupees ($1.94) per kg from 116.33 last week, Forbes and Walker said.
Better westerns gained two to three rupees per kilo, but other varieties of high growns were barely firm and poor quality highs declined by two to three rupees, brokers said.
